name: Venmo Business Profiles
description: Venmo Business Profiles let eligible businesses receive commercial payments under a business identity. The documented developer surface is primarily merchant checkout through PayPal or Braintree, with Venmo as a user-authorized US payment method, rather than a general Business Profile ledger or account-administration API.
agentUseSummary: Venmo Business Profiles cannot yet be connected through Relay. Merchant integrations require an eligible US business model, PayPal or Braintree merchant account, compatible checkout SDK, selected Business Profile where supported, user authorization, order processing, settlement, refund, dispute, and compliance controls. Relay has no approved business profile, processor, checkout, catalog, amount, vaulting, refund, dispute, or financial-authority contract.

blocked.label: Connect a Venmo Business Profile
blocked.description: An eligible US business, approved PayPal or Braintree merchant account, selected Business Profile, processor configuration, and compatible checkout are required.

blocked.label: Present Venmo checkout
blocked.description: Eligibility checks, buttons, app handoff, payment authorization, addresses, one-time payments, and saved payment methods remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Process Venmo transactions
blocked.description: Creating orders, authorizing, capturing, vaulting, charging, refunding, disputing, settling, transferring, or otherwise moving money is blocked.

blocked.label: Access Business Profile account data
blocked.description: Profiles, customers, balances, bank accounts, cards, transaction history, statements, tax records, social feeds, contacts, and unrelated Venmo data are unavailable.

blocked.label: Use private or credential-based access
blocked.description: Venmo app or browser automation, password or session capture, payment-sheet automation, unapproved merchant credentials, and private APIs are blocked.

providerSetup.blocker: The supported developer path for Venmo commerce is a user-authorized payment method embedded in an eligible merchant's PayPal Checkout or Braintree integration, not a generic Business Profile account API. PayPal requires a business account and checkout integration; Venmo is US-only, eligibility-dependent, and not displayed by default. Braintree limits merchant Venmo to supported business models and compatible web or mobile SDKs, and explicitly excludes in-person collection, post-service app collection, and peer-to-peer facilitation. Some flows can vault Venmo for future merchant charges or route transactions to a selected Business Profile, which adds durable payment authority. A generic agent tool would obscure the merchant, buyer consent, order, processor, profile, settlement, refund, dispute, and vaulting boundaries.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, commerce, payments, finance, legal, privacy, security, PCI, fraud, support, tax, and business owners must select one supported US checkout and freeze the legal merchant, Business Profile, processor, SDK, catalog, pricing, taxes, shipping, user handoff, order validation, vaulting, amount and velocity limits, authorization, capture, fulfillment, refunds, disputes, settlement, reconciliation, retention, audit, and incident duties. The merchant must then complete PayPal or Braintree onboarding and Venmo eligibility. Only after that may Relay support a customer-facing checkout with server-verified orders and explicit payer authorization; no unattended agent money movement should be mounted.

evidence.supports: Pay with Venmo requires a PayPal business account and Checkout integration, is US-only, and uses a Venmo app user experience and explicit funding-source enablement.
Braintree Venmo checkout is limited to eligible US businesses and compatible SDKs and excludes in-person, post-service app, and peer-to-peer uses.
Braintree merchant integrations can select a Venmo Business Profile for a transaction using its profile identifier.
PayPal documents Venmo as a US digital-wallet checkout payment method with refunds, not a general profile-data API.
Supported checkout flows can save Venmo payment methods for future merchant use, creating durable charge authority that requires explicit controls.
